message.content: Lions mate in a relatively straightforward but highly social way. Male lions typically form coalitions—groups of related males that defend a pride together. When a coalition approaches a pride, they will often engage in a display of dominance and vocalization (roaring) to establish their presence. If the females are receptive, the males will engage in a brief but intense mating ritual. This usually involves the male mounting the female from behind, positioning his hind legs around her hips, and using his forepaws to hold her in place. The actual copulation lasts only a few minutes, during which the male may perform a series of thrusts. After mating, the male will leave the pride, as lions are polygynous and do not guard the offspring. The female will then give birth after a gestation period of about 110 days.
